The core operator 'copy_certainty_verification' enforces that all copy assertions are grounded in prior build card evidence and validated in the real application. This is modeled as a Bayesian update where certainty C is conditioned on evidence E and repo state R. When these conditions fail, a launch blocker is triggered. The 'launch_readiness_condition' ensures that new work references rather than duplicates prior efforts, maintaining a clean kernel of development. The 'brand_voice_assurance' primitive enforces linguistic integrity by ensuring guarantees, tout language, and overclaims are absent. These three primitives form a triadic constraint system that governs product surface trustworthiness and launch readiness. Failure in any one leads to degradation in downstream metrics such as user trust, revenue, and support efficiency. The system's robustness relies on the interplay between evidence integrity, duplication control, and linguistic fidelity.
